subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics Standard, Year 11
about: HSC, Algebra, money, measurement, networks and data
syllabus: NSW Mathematics Standard 11-12 Syllabus (2024), Year 11 focus areas (common to Standard 1 and 2)

points.title: Substituting into formulas
points.brief: Replacing the letters in a formula with numbers and working it out in the right order, such as finding speed from distance and time.

points.title: Changing the subject of a formula
points.brief: Rearranging a formula to make a different letter the subject, by doing the same operation to both sides.

points.title: Solving linear equations
points.brief: Solving equations with one unknown, including brackets and fractions, by undoing operations in reverse order and checking the answer.

points.title: Formulas with units
points.brief: Keeping units consistent when substituting, such as converting minutes to hours before using a speed formula.

points.title: Writing equations from words
points.brief: Turning a worded situation into an equation, such as a phone plan with a fixed fee plus a cost per gigabyte, then solving it.

points.title: Gradient as a rate of change
points.brief: The gradient is rise over run and, in context, a rate, such as dollars per hour or litres per minute.

points.title: The y-intercept in context
points.brief: The value of y when x is zero, often a starting amount or fixed cost, such as a call-out fee.

points.title: The equation y = mx + c
points.brief: Writing and graphing a linear equation from its gradient and y-intercept, and reading them off a graph.

points.title: Direct variation
points.brief: When y = kx, y is directly proportional to x. The graph is a straight line through the origin and k is the constant of variation.

points.title: Linear models
points.brief: Using a straight-line model to make predictions, such as the cost of a taxi ride, and knowing that a model may stop being accurate outside the data.

points.title: Wages and salaries
points.brief: A wage is paid per hour worked. A salary is a fixed amount per year, often paid weekly, fortnightly or monthly. Converting between them.

points.title: Overtime and penalty rates
points.brief: Extra pay for work outside normal hours, such as time-and-a-half or double time, and working out total pay.

points.title: Commission and piecework
points.brief: Commission is a percentage of sales. Piecework pays a fixed amount per item made or task done.

points.title: Taxable income
points.brief: Gross income minus allowable deductions gives taxable income, which income tax is worked out on.

points.title: Income tax and net pay
points.brief: Using a tax table with brackets to find income tax, adding the Medicare levy, and working out take-home pay after tax and other deductions.

points.title: Budgeting
points.brief: Listing income and expenses to plan spending and saving, and telling fixed costs, such as rent, from variable costs, such as food.

points.title: Simple interest
points.brief: I = Prn, where interest is earned or charged only on the starting amount.

points.title: Compound interest by repeated calculation
points.brief: Interest added to the balance each period so it earns interest too. Working it out period by period shows how it grows faster than simple interest.

points.title: Percentage increase and decrease
points.brief: Finding a new amount after a percentage change, and working backwards to an original price, such as a price before a discount.

points.title: GST
points.brief: Australia's Goods and Services Tax is 10% on most goods and services. Adding it, and finding the GST in a price that already includes it by dividing by 11.

points.title: Household bills
points.brief: Reading electricity, water and phone bills, including fixed supply charges and charges per unit used, and comparing plans.

points.title: Accuracy of measurements
points.brief: Every measurement has limits. The absolute error is half the smallest unit on the instrument, and the limits of accuracy are the measurement plus or minus that.

points.title: Significant figures and scientific notation
points.brief: Rounding to significant figures and writing very large or small numbers as a number between 1 and 10 times a power of ten.

points.title: Unit conversions
points.brief: Converting lengths, areas, volumes, masses and capacities between units, such as cm² to m², and remembering that 1 cm³ holds 1 mL.

points.title: Perimeter and area
points.brief: Perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, circles, trapeziums and shapes made of these.

points.title: Surface area
points.brief: The total area of all the faces of a solid, such as a prism or cylinder, found by adding the area of each face.

points.title: Volume and capacity
points.brief: Volume of prisms and cylinders as base area times height, and capacity as how much liquid a container holds.

points.title: Latitude and longitude
points.brief: Latitude measures degrees north or south of the equator. Longitude measures degrees east or west of the prime meridian through Greenwich. Together they locate any place.

points.title: Time zones
points.brief: The world is divided into time zones measured from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Sydney is UTC+10, or UTC+11 during daylight saving.

points.title: Longitude and time difference
points.brief: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so 15° of longitude is about one hour of time difference.

points.title: Travel across time zones
points.brief: Working out arrival times for flights that cross time zones, adding the flight time and the time difference.

points.title: The International Date Line
points.brief: Crossing the date line going west adds a day, and going east takes a day away.

points.title: Network terms
points.brief: A network has vertices joined by edges. The degree of a vertex is how many edges meet there, and a weighted network has values on its edges, such as distances.

points.title: Walks, paths and circuits
points.brief: A walk is any route along edges. A path never repeats a vertex. A circuit starts and ends at the same vertex.

points.title: Shortest paths
points.brief: Finding the route of least total weight between two vertices by checking possible routes or using a step-by-step method.

points.title: Trees
points.brief: A tree is a connected network with no circuits. A tree with n vertices has n - 1 edges.

points.title: Minimum spanning trees
points.brief: The tree that connects every vertex with the least total weight, found with Prim's or Kruskal's method, such as for laying cable.

points.title: The statistical investigation process
points.brief: Posing a question, collecting data, organising and displaying it, analysing it and drawing a conclusion that answers the question.

points.title: Sampling methods
points.brief: Random, systematic, stratified and self-selected samples, and how a poor sample can bias the results.

points.title: Categorical and numerical data
points.brief: Categorical data names groups and numerical data counts or measures. Numerical data is discrete (counts) or continuous (measures).

points.title: Displaying data
points.brief: Dot plots, histograms, stem-and-leaf plots and column graphs, and choosing one that suits the data.

points.title: Mean, median and mode
points.brief: Three measures of centre, and when each gives a fair picture. Outliers pull the mean but barely move the median.

points.title: Spread and box plots
points.brief: Range, quartiles and interquartile range, shown on a box plot, used to compare two sets of data.
